figures.1: Figure 1. Reference-space performance is evaluated against complete non-reference alleles. a, Paired alleles share their flanks; ALT contains the complete natural insertion. b, The approved Class B catalogue contains 32969 loci, from which 400 core loci targeting 387 genes were frozen without model outcomes. Both models yield finite homologous-exon scores at 318 loci; the remaining 82 lack common scorable exon support and remain in the denominator. c, AlphaGenome and Borzoi each score the complete REF and ALT alleles on the same retained homologous exon bases; ΔRNA is ALT minus REF per-base RNA density. d, Technical reproducibility, cross-model reliability and biological calibration address distinct questions. e, Frozen reference, original insertion and reference-minus-insertion rank estimates summarize the main contrast; GNRS yields 9/33 jointly usable loci. Shared flanks denote locus-specific callable absence, not genome-wide sequence uniqueness. The benchmarks are nonmatched, and the gap is not a causal estimate of reference absence. Source data are provided in the Figure 1 source-data files.
figures.2: Figure 2. Cross-model agreement remains limited across off-reference RNA scoring definitions. a, Original AlphaGenome and Borzoi ΔRNA values for all 318 jointly finite loci. Points are untransformed and in model-specific per-base density units. Thin zero guides indicate no predicted effect. The inset enlarges the central region (AlphaGenome −0.001 to 0.001; Borzoi −0.003 to 0.003); the main plot retains every finite point and the full range. b, Rank agreement and nonzero-sign concordance with their frozen 95% confidence intervals (CIs). c, Rank agreement across original, cached exact-family, newly strict, near-family and full-RNA definitions; the adjacent column reports sign concordance. All definitions retain 318 jointly finite and nonzero pairs from the 400 frozen loci. Intervals use 10000 paired-locus bootstrap resamples. The 50% sign guide is descriptive and does not establish random performance or equivalence. No outliers were removed, axes broken or values winsorized. Source data retain all 400 identities and unavailable scores.
figures.3: Figure 3. Within-model placement robustness coexists with official-member sensitivity and limited cross-model agreement. a, The same complete allele is evaluated at baseline and prespecified −32768-bp and +32768-bp placements. b, Rank stability versus baseline for each model and shift; points and thin lines show estimates and frozen 95% paired-locus bootstrap CIs (10000 resamples). Labels give sign concordance. Each comparison uses 72/100 fixed-common-support loci. c, Dominant nonzero-sign fraction across four official members at 77/100 loci per model. Deterministic horizontal offsets reveal coincident observations; short horizontal lines mark the frozen median of 0.75. Non-unanimous fractions are 87.0% for AlphaGenome and 90.9% for Borzoi. Members are alternative fitted models, not biological replicates. d, Placement stability and limited cross-model reliability summarize different evidence. Blue circles denote AlphaGenome and grey squares Borzoi. The four frozen post-hoc illustrative loci are retained in Supplementary Figure S12. Source data include all frozen identities and unavailable settings.
figures.4: Figure 4. Prediction stability decreases under restricted sequence context. a, AlphaGenome uses native 16384-bp and 131072-bp inputs relative to its 1048576-bp baseline. Borzoi retains 16384 or 131072 bp within a 524288-bp native input and replaces outside sequence with N bases. These interventions differ. b, Rank stability and c, sign concordance relative to each model’s native baseline, using the same 29 jointly usable loci from the fixed 100-locus subset. Blue circles and solid lines denote AlphaGenome; grey squares and dashed lines denote Borzoi. Thin intervals are frozen 95% CIs from 10000 paired-locus bootstrap resamples. Hollow native points are self-comparison identities (ρ = 1; sign = 100%), without estimated CIs. Context positions are categorical, not a shared physical-distance scale. d, Untransformed AlphaGenome 16384-bp versus native effects show all 29 finite pairs in model-specific density units; the other three scatter comparisons are retained in Supplementary Figure S13. CIs describe each restricted-versus-native comparison and do not test the two restricted lengths against one another. Context sensitivity does not establish a long-range biological cause of model disagreement. Source data retain all 100 identities and settings.
figures.5: Figure 5. Model agreement is lower for complete insertions than for the reference-coordinate comparator. a, The nonmatched benchmarks comprise 500 high-PIP reference SNVs spanning 473 genes and 400 complete Class B insertions spanning 387 genes, with 318 jointly finite insertion pairs. b, Reference and c, original insertion cross-model ΔRNA values; all finite points and their full ranges are retained, with model-specific density units and thin zero guides. d, Rank and e, nonzero-sign agreement with frozen 95% bootstrap CIs; slate circles denote reference and teal diamonds insertions. The 50% sign guide is descriptive. The displayed reference-minus-insertion gaps are Δρ = 0.737 (95% CI 0.574–0.897) and 21.3 percentage points (pp; 95% CI 14.6–28.2). Reference uncertainty resamples 473 gene clusters; insertion uncertainty resamples 318 paired loci. Gap CIs use independent 10000-resample reference-gene and insertion-locus streams. The contrast uses reference strict and core cached exact-family endpoints; the latter reproduces the original core estimate. f, Variant class, ascertainment and other benchmark characteristics differ. The contrast describes a benchmark generalization gap and does not isolate a causal effect of reference absence. Measured reference calibration remains in Table 2. Source data include raw effects, complete denominators and unrounded gap estimates.
figures.6: Figure 6. Independent biological calibration of complete insertions remains incomplete. a, Gene-preserving GNRS recovery yields 9 jointly usable loci from 33 frozen insertion–gene pairs. The dashed side annotation is the theoretical Borzoi geometry maximum of 13, not an observed recovery stage. b, Nonzero-sign concordance with measured insertion-presence direction: AlphaGenome 2/9 (22.2%) and Borzoi 5/9 (55.6%). Blue circles and grey squares have frozen 95% paired-locus bootstrap CIs (10000 resamples); the 50% guide is descriptive. These results are below the prespecified N = 20 calibration gate and cannot rank biological accuracy. c, The external public table contains 13272 association rows; 1994 anchor/length candidate rows link to 558 loci in the broader Class B catalogue. Row and locus counts are different units. Exact insertion sequence, effect orientation and independent signed truth remain unresolved; this is not negative biological evidence or additional validated core truth. d, Established observations and unresolved questions are separated. e, The five-level evidence framework documents sequence and coordinate validity, assesses technical robustness and cross-model reliability, and leaves biological calibration incomplete. Level 4 is assessed with limited agreement, not passed. These levels are an evidence framework, not a new composite score. Source data are supplied for all panels.

table_notes.1: Counts describe frozen variants and target genes. Insertion length and repeat summaries use all 400 core loci. Joint finite scores require homologous-exon RNA effects from both models. The GNRS panel is separate from the core. Reference and off-reference benchmarks were nonmatched. NA indicates unavailable in the frozen comparator, not biological absence. Discovery AF is ALT/called haplotypes, not population prevalence.
table_notes.2: N is finite/frozen variants or loci; finite and nonzero-sign denominators are identical for retained rows. Except for placement ranges, parentheses give frozen 95% bootstrap CIs: 10000 paired-locus resamples for insertion/context endpoints and 10000 gene-cluster resamples for reference endpoints. ¹ Placement entries report the range of two prespecified shifts (−32768 and +32768 bp), not a CI or pooled estimate; direction-specific CIs remain in Figure 3b and Supplementary Table S12. Context comparisons are versus native baseline; Borzoi uses N-mask ablation. Gap CIs use independent reference-gene and core-locus streams and the cached exact-family insertion endpoint. pp, percentage points; —, inapplicable. The gap is nonmatched and noncausal. Full sensitivity rows and descriptive GNRS N=9 estimates are retained in Supplementary Table S12.
